author: ALM
body:
When the world type is normal, there is a very ugly horizon line that appears at y 80. Below this point, the sky turns black and looks very bad.
If the world type is set to Superflat, the line occurs at y -4 which is fine since no blocks can be placed at this level. 
My suggestion is that all maps be set to Superflat so this line does not happen.

Thoughts?

replies.author: MasterProX
replies.body:
That's not what he means. He's suggesting that maps should be built in worlds that have been generated with the "superflat" world type as opposed to the "default" type (what I mean by "world types"). Apparently, the horizon line is positioned differently in superflat worlds, probably to accommodate for the lack of a standard sea level — usually around Y: 62 — upon which regularly generated worlds place the horizon... or something like that. Most, if not all, Avicus maps currently in the repository were created in a default template, though the natural terrain was deleted in favor of a floating map surrounded by air on all sides; obviously, there's no more ocean in the world file, but the horizon is still there, and as a result, there's a very noticeable and unsightly demarcation spanning the entire length of the sky (as seen here). This has nothing to do with the altitude of the map itself.

While editing all the existing maps to reflect this change would indeed be nice, I don't think the map developers would enjoy taking the time to do that, nor is this any sort of exigent concern that would make any practical, non-aesthetic difference. To reiterate, who notices — or even cares about — the horizon of a map when playing Nebula?
